Morgan (AE): Eva asked us to formalize the POC acceptance criteria today. High level ask: 4-week sandbox, production-like traffic, and security sign-off. Their immediate targets:
- perf: p95 latency <= 300ms for single-turn requests under peak profile
- cost: target <= $350 per 1M request-equivalents (tokenized)
- quality: golden-set ROUGE-L drop <= 1.5% and MRR drop <= 0.02 vs their current system
They also want KMS + SSO + audit retention covered before kickoff.

Sam (SE): good. need traffic profile to size the pool and pick batching params. also want the prompt/eval suite (golden set) to baseline accuracy.

Eva (Buyer): traffic: sustained 20 qps, peak bursts to 70 qps for a few minutes, average input ~140 tokens, average output ~80, tail cases up to 1500 tokens for retrieval-augmented flows (rare). Monthly projected requests ~1.05M.

Diego (Eng): recommendation: start on hosted canary for 48h midday window with an identical workload generator, then spin up a dedicated mini-pool (1x H100 equivalent) with burst autoscaling to 2 nodes if peak observed. We'll include an FP16 and 8-bit quantized run so you can evaluate cost/quality tradeoffs.

Sam (SE): perf test sketch to run (please paste in harness):
```
scenario: mixed
sustained_qps: 20
peak_qps: 70
median_seq_len: 220
p95_seq_len: 820
duration: 3h
metrics: p50,p95,p99,errors,token_burn
```
Use p95 as primary gate.

Morgan (AE): propose three acceptance gates for go/no-go:
A) Perf gate: p95 <= 300ms over a rolling 48h canary window with error rate <0.5% and no sustained throttling.
B) Cost gate: modeled monthly burn (using their 1.05M projection) <= $350 / 1M equiv (we'll show tokenization calc + sensitivity for quantized path).
C) Quality gate: golden-set ROUGE-L drop <=1.5% and MRR delta <=0.02 on the evaluation harness; if quantized model used, must still meet these thresholds.
If any gate fails, we default to the customer's current ensemble and open an ops postmortem.

Eva (Buyer): for cost gate, we need an explicit breakdown (reserved vs hosted, baseline commit pricing). Can you show both: committed-dedicated and hosted-payg? Also SLA ask: 99.9% uptime during trial.

Diego (Eng): will produce a cost sheet with two scenarios: (1) hosted pay-as-you-go, (2) dedicated reserved (1 node + burst). I'll include expected latency profiles per scenario and the sensitivity to batching window. SLA during trial: we can commit to operational runbook and 99.9% availability for dedicated pool; hosted has best-effort but we can add monitoring and alerts.

Sam (SE): security checklist: KMS flow (customer-owned CMK or Redwood-managed), SSO (SAML/OIDC), audit retention windows (30/90/365 days), and SOC2 excerpt. sec-bot: please attach the SOC2 summary and sample KMS wiring doc.

sec-bot: attached: soc2-summary.pdf (internal), kms-wiring-diagram.png, sample-saml-flow.txt :white_check_mark: 

Morgan (AE): timeline & action items:
- Today EOD: Sam uploads golden-set and KMS diagram; Diego posts cost scenarios; sec-bot attaches SOC2 excerpt.
- +48h: perf run completed, post results (p95 and token burn).
- +72h: send finalized acceptance doc to Eva and schedule 30-min gate review.
Owners: Sam (golden-set & runbook), Diego (cost sheet & infra config), Morgan (customer comms / acceptance doc).

Diego (Eng): one implementation note: 8-bit gives ~1.5-1.8x throughput for decoding-heavy workloads but can introduce small ROUGE variance. We'll include both runs in the eval and flag any cases where the golden-set degrades >1%.

Eva (Buyer): that works. Please make the acceptance doc explicit about rollback triggers and who to notify. Also include a data handling appendix for the RAG content.

Morgan (AE): will add rollback contacts and the data-handling appendix. Thanks team — I'll update once assets are in and book the review meeting. :rocket:
